dataset.name: Advanced non-TCGA thyroid cancer cohort (META-PRISM, 2023)
dataset.description: Histology-specific thyroid cancer subset of the independent META-PRISM refractory and metastatic pan-cancer cohort with public gene-level TPM and individual overall survival.
dataset.cohort_context: Advanced, refractory or metastatic thyroid cancer sampled during precision-oncology care. Nine of ten patients have medullary thyroid carcinoma and one has poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma; this release expands histologic coverage and is not population-matched to primary papillary TCGA-THCA.

metadata.study_design: Prospective molecular profiling of refractory or metastatic adult cancers
metadata.source_data_system: Gustave Roussy cBioPortal and public Nextcloud data release
metadata.source_platform: Bulk RNA-seq quantified with Kallisto v0.44.0 and tximport v1.16.0
metadata.endpoint_context: Overall survival recorded by the source study
metadata.redistribution_note: The processed TPM matrix is publicly downloadable and analyzable in TRACE Explorer. Direct redistribution remains disabled because the public release does not state a standard redistribution license.
metadata.curation_note: The release includes only the source-defined THCA - Not_TCGA cohort. RNASEQ_SAMPLE_ID is required to link each cBioPortal clinical sample deterministically to one TPM column. This is a small advanced-disease histology expansion, not an external replication cohort for papillary TCGA-THCA.

samples.sample_role: Biopsy from advanced, refractory or metastatic thyroid cancer

expression.label: META-PRISM TPM transformed as log2(TPM + 1)
expression.mapping_source: Pinned GENCODE release 27 annotation declared by META-PRISM
expression.duplicate_feature_rationale: Ensembl identifiers mapping to a duplicated case-normalized gene symbol are excluded rather than combined without a source-defined aggregation rule.
expression.scale_note: The source publishes Kallisto and tximport gene-level TPM against GENCODE v27. TRACE Explorer applies log2(TPM + 1) without cross-study renormalization; values are suitable for within-cohort analysis only.
